faq.a: Samia is associated with the Arabic form سَامِيَة, whose core sense is samia; elevated, lofty (feminine).

faq.q: What is the origin of Samia?
faq.a: Samia is associated with Arabic. Samia is Arabic سَامِيَة (Sāmiya), the feminine of سَامِي, meaning 'elevated, lofty'.
Yes — the underlying form سَامِيَة is Arabic.
Samia can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Samia should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Sāmiya is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.a: Romanization variants include Samia, samia. Script forms are ساميه, سامیه, سامیہ, سَامِيَة, सामिया.

faq.q: Is Samia a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
